newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congress considers $5.3 billion disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congress considers $5.3 billion disaster aid.

text.p: Congress will consider an emergency spending bill to provide $5.3 billion for disaster relief in more than 20 states and $2 billion for peacekeeping forces in Bosnia, the House Appropriations Committee said on Friday.

Committee chairman Bob Livingston said the extra spending will be paid for by cutting a host of other government activities, the largest of which will be $3.6 billion taken from Housing Department funds.

Livingston, a Louisiana Republican, said he expected the funding bill would move quickly through the House. The panel is to vote on it next Thursday, after which it will go to the full House and then on to the Senate.
The money for U.S. troops will pay for past activities and does not signify congressional acceptance of continued U.S. presence in Bosnia.
Congress will also take the opportunity to add nearly $100 million for non-emergency funds including $1.7 million to help the Federal Election Commission upgrade its computers.
President Bill Clinton has received only half the $76 billion he requested for the Women, Infants and Children feeding program for poor families.

Democrats warned that hundreds of thousands could lose aid, but Republicans charged that the administration padded its spending plan. The panel said there were ample funds that were expected to be carried over into next year.
The military funds include $1.35 billion for peacekeeping in Bosnia and $562 million for Southwest Asia. These efforts were paid for by cuts in 60 other military programs.
